title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 39-40
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 39 to 40 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 39 to 40 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 39 to 40.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 39 to 40** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः । सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो लक्ष्मीवान् समितिञ्जयः ॥** **विक्षरो रोहितो मार्गो हेतुर्दामोदरः सहः । महीधरो महाभागो वेगवानमिताशनः ॥**

He has no equal, he is Sharabha, terrible to the wicked. The knower of the right time, Hari who accepts the offerings, is that God of gods. Marked by every auspicious sign, lord of Lakshmi, victor in every battle. He does not decay, he is rosy in hue and he is the path itself. The cause of all, Damodara, the patient one, is that God of gods. He bears the earth, of great fortune and swift, accepting offerings without limit.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 39 to 40 mean?
faq.a: He has no equal, he is Sharabha, terrible to the wicked. The knower of the right time, Hari who accepts the offerings, is that God of gods. Marked by every auspicious sign, lord of Lakshmi, victor in every battle. He does not decay, he is rosy in hue and he is the path itself. The cause of all, Damodara, the patient one, is that God of gods. He bears the earth, of great fortune and swift, accepting offerings without limit.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
